title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Which read audit row of a refused get query holds the refusal code?
description: ST-SUP-RP11-LC17 says that Serve gives the code of a declared refusal to the read audit row, and ST-SUP-RP11-LC17-T02 expects the code order.unknown in the read audit row. But the query runtime writes the read audit row of each resource of personal data when the fill reads it, before the value reaches the fill (ST-SUP-RP11-LC08), so the row is written with the outcome ok before the fill returns its refusal; and a refusal of a fill that read no personal data has no read audit row at all. Options: (a) the read audit rows stay as the reads were, and the refusal code goes to the problem response and the completion log only; change ST-SUP-RP11-LC17 and its test T02 to say so; (b) Run also writes one failed read audit row with the refusal code for each resource of personal data that the fill read, after the ok row of the read, which doubles the rows of such a resource; (c) the query declaration names its resource entity, and Serve writes one failed read audit row with the code on the requested resource, also for an entity with no personal data. Recommendation: (a): a read audit row records a read, and the read took place; the refusal is an outcome of the request, which the completion log and the problem response hold.

title: Which runtime helper serves the commands of generated CRUD, whose bodies are JSON?
description: ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05 puts code that is the same for every declaration in the runtime library, and command.Serve (ST-SUP-RP10-LC33) serves a command whose request and response are protobuf messages. The handlers of generated CRUD on the runtime data path (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37) decode JSON, run the bound slots around Run and answer with the problem types of the rest-api component, so they cannot use command.Serve, and they still emit the same steps for every declaration: the bind of the verified tenant and principal, the map of an error of Run to its status, code and audit outcome, and the outcome audit row (command.RunHelpers of the command generator). The runtime has no exported helper for these steps. Options: (a) the command runtime exports the bind (BindIdentity), the outcome map (OutcomeOf) and the outcome row of a request, which command.Serve uses itself, and generated CRUD calls them; (b) the command runtime gives a second serving helper for JSON bodies with hooks for the slots; (c) generated CRUD keeps emitting these steps. Recommendation: (a): the steps then have one source with tests in the runtime, and the slots, which vary with the declaration, stay in the generated code.
